newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called off on technical weakness.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called off on technical weakness.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called off on technical weakness Friday after a failing at a session high Thursday to settle lower.
"Crude is basically down because it made a higher high yesterday but then failed to follow-through and closed lower, which puts it in a bad position," said one chartist.
Crude was called off five to 10 cents a barrel. Heating oil was called unchanged to 0.25 cent off a gallon and gasoline was called off 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.
State regulators said Tosco restarted its 140,000 bpd catalytic cracker at its Bayway refinery in Linden, N.J.

Regulators said the restart began Wednesday after the unit, the largest cat cracker in the world, was shut down in early January to undergo maintenance following a fire-related outage in early December. The refinery has a total capacity of 290,000 bpd. However, one trader said he had heard the restart was having difficulty.
"I heard they are having problems with catalysts being released," said the dealer. Tosco declined comment.
On Thursday, March crude ended off six cents a barrel at $24.18 after rising as high as to $24.75 intraday. Feb heat ended off 0.54 cent a gallon at 66.35 cents.
Feb gasoline ended up 0.20 cent a gallon at 68.42 cents.

"I don't think the Tosco news will have any negative impact on the crack spread," said one gasoline dealer, noting gasoline's crack spread is attracting considerble buying interest ahead of the spring and summer season when gasoline demand traditionally peaks.
Also supportive to gasoline was the shut down of Exxon Corp's 88,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracker at its Baytown, Texas refinery for scheduled maintenance.
Meanwhile, dealers pegged Fibonacci support for prompt crude at $23.89, representing 50 percent retracement of March's move from its November low of $21.72 to its contract high of $26.05 January 9.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
